item.title: Alleged Chinese agent makes federal court appearance
item.description: CBS News was first to report​ that the FBI arrested Wanying "Heather" Zhang on Sunday at Los Angeles International Airport before she boarded a flight to Shanghai, China.

item.title: U.S. and German scientists win Nobel Price in medicine for discoveries on optogenetics
item.description: American Karl Deisseroth, a neuroscientist and psychiatrist, has won the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, along with two German scientists. Their discoveries in optogenetics could reshape how we study the brain and understand how it processes information. Dr. Heather Berlin, an associate professor of psychiatry and neuroscience at Mount Sinai, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: FBI arrests woman at LAX accused of being Chinese agent
item.description: Wanying "Heather" Zhang, an Irvine, California, realtor, was arrested on a charge of acting as an unregistered agent of a foreign government.

item.title: Alleged Chinese agent arrested in Los Angeles after allegedly surveilling son of Taiwanese president
item.description: A suspected Chinese agent appeared in court Monday after allegedly surveilling the son of the Taiwanese president. The FBI arrested Wanying "Heather" Zhang on Sunday as she was preparing to board a flight from Los Angeles International Airport to Shanghai. CBS News homeland security correspondent Nicole Sganga reports.

item.title: After B-1 bomber removal, Rubio says administration still has confidence in all international bases
item.description: The U.S. Air Force has removed all of its bombers from a U.K. air base following a security incident there last month. CBS News national security correspondent Charlie D'Agata has more.

item.title: Inside the cases the Supreme Court will take up this term
item.description: The Supreme Court's new term kicked off on Monday and the justices are expected to weigh in on issues from voting rights to gun control. The first case of this term examines whether federal law prevents state and local governments from holding oil companies liable in climate disputes. CBS News legal reporter Kartina Kaufman has a preview of the biggest cases.

item.title: Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan to be executed by firing squad, Pentagon says
item.description: The Trump administration has approved a plan to execute former Army Maj. Nidal Hasan — who killed 13 people in a 2009 shooting at Fort Hood — by firing squad, the Pentagon said.

item.title: Susan Collins and Troy Jackson tied in new poll as Jeffries praises Democrats' midterm prospects
item.description: The latest CBS News and YouGov polling shows that Republican incumbent Sen. Susan Collins and Democratic challenger Troy Jackson are running virtually neck-and-neck in Maine's highly-watched Senate race. CBS News congressional correspondent Nikole Killion reports.

item.title: Alito slams criticism of Supreme Court from political leaders, says it can be "quite damaging"
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito told CBS News he thinks criticism of the Supreme Court from political leaders can be "quite damaging." CBS News legal contributor Jessica Levinson shares her thoughts on the interview and the upcoming docket for the high court as it begins a new term.

item.title: Extended Interview: Sen. Thom Tillis
item.description: In an extended interview with 60 Minutes correspondent Ross Douthat, Sen. Thom Tillis details why he considers some in President Trump's inner circle "sycophants," and also discusses the Iran war and what awaits the Republican party in the midterms and 2028.

item.title: Battle with Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen tempers news on oil flow
item.description: Brent crude hovers around $100 a barrel despite news of increased Mideast oil flows, as Iran's Houthi allies battle over control of Red Sea shipping lanes.

item.title: Defense attorney says Letitia James should recuse herself from Cornell probe
item.description: An attorney for one of the men accused in the alleged sexual assault of a former Cornell University student​ in 2024 is calling for Attorney General Letitia James to step down as special prosecutor.

item.title: Medical expert on reported plague lab death in Russia
item.description: CBS News medical correspondent Dr. Céline Gounder shares her thoughts and breaks down what we know about a reported plague lab death in Russia.

item.title: College sports tradition "Hawkeye Wave" reaches new high, as opposing team gets involved
item.description: The "Hawkeye Wave" happens at every Iowa Hawkeyes home football game, where the entire stadium turns away and waves at the kids in the windows of the neighboring children's hospital. Tony Dokoupil has the story.

item.title: Ex-"American Idol" contestant Caleb Flynn gets life sentence
item.description: Caleb Flynn was found guilty of killing his wife, Ashley, and attempting to blame the murder on a break-in at their home.

item.title: Former "American Idol" contestant proclaims his innocence during sentencing for wife's murder
item.description: Former music pastor and "American Idol" contestant received a life sentence on Monday for the execution-style murder of his wife. But as Jericka Duncan reports, he was still claiming his innocence as he was sentenced.

item.title: Justice Alito on the Supreme Court: "We are not part of any political movement"
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito gave a rare interview to CBS News chief legal correspondent Jan Crawford. He said it is wrong for leaders of both parties to portray the justices as political players.

item.title: U.S. military removes bombers from U.K. air base following security incident
item.description: All U.S. bombers deployed to RAF Fairford have been returned to their home stations in the United States, a Pentagon spokesperson confirmed to CBS News.

item.title: Trump focuses on securing red states ahead of midterms
item.description: Election Day is four weeks from Tuesday and President Trump is back on the campaign trail, not in an effort to gain ground on Democrats, but to protect what has historically been Republican-friendly territory. Ed O'Keefe reports from Nebraska.

item.title: Russia plays down reported plague lab death and says, trust us
item.description: A Russian plague lab worker died of "pneumonia of unknown origin," officials say, in response to initial reports that she was exposed to the deadly bacteria during a lab accident.

item.title: Israel scrambled jets, was prepared to shoot down FlyDubai flight after pilot attack, sources say
item.description: Israeli sources say they were prepared to shoot down last week's FlyDubai flight where a co-pilot allegedly attacked the flight's captain, even though there were more than 150 Israeli passengers on board. CBS News' Matt Gutman reports.

item.title: What to know as Trump continues midterm campaign push, urges supporters to vote by mail
item.description: President Trump is continuing to hit the campaign trail for Republican candidates with the midterm elections less than a month away. CBS News' Ed O'Keefe and Anthony Salvanto have more.

item.title: 1 student dead, another person killed in Florida school bus crash
item.description: A school bus with 37 students on board flipped over onto its roof in a multi-vehicle accident. One student died on Monday and everyone else on board was rushed to the hospital. According to investigators, a driver crossed the center line and crashed into the side of the bus, sending it into oncoming traffic and killing at least one other driver. Cristian Benavides reports.

item.title: JD Vance says he thinks Ted Cruz is running for president, Cruz calls Vance insecure
item.description: Vice President JD Vance said late last week that he thinks Sen. Ted Cruz is running for president. Cruz responded by saying he's focused on the midterms and thinks Vance is insecure. Ofirah Yheskel, director of external affairs for the Democratic Governors Association, and Manhattan Institute Vice President Jesse Arm join "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: 10/5: CBS Evening News
item.description: 2 were killed and dozens were injured in a Florida school bus crash; a lab worker died from suspected plague exposure in Russia.

item.title: Coca-Cola reveals new flavors for Coke, Powerade and other brands
item.description: Coca-Cola said it will roll out the new flavors, all fruit-inspired, in 2027. Here's what the beverage giant is planning.

item.title: 10/5: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Trump urges supporters to vote by mail as midterms near; Supreme Court hears arguments from oil companies attempting to end climate change lawsuits.

item.title: Gatorade sold in dozens of states recalled due to undeclared dyes
item.description: Recalled Gatorade sold in 37 states could cause temporary "adverse health consequences," a federal regulatory agency says.

item.title: Experts are training AI on how to do their jobs
item.description: It's become a booming industry: teaching artificial intelligence how to get better at doing all kinds of jobs. As AI advances, many fear what this tech means for the future of work.

item.title: "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" guests for Oct. 4, 2026
item.description: This week's guests include Energy Secretary Chris Wright and Democratic Sen. Mark Kelly.
